page: Vultr vx1-m-2c-16g-120s is a memory-optimized virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads. The hardware includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core allocation. Local storage is provided via a bundled 120 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression and decompression tasks scoring in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, while small-block read-only bandwidth is weak. Static web serving throughput is average at 6.5 GB/sec, whereas database operations and Redis SET operations perform in the bottom 25%.

This server offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without intensive multi-threaded processing. The primary tradeoff is the weak multi-core scaling and database performance, which limits its utility for heavy parallel computing or high-throughput transactional databases. It is best suited for memory-intensive single-threaded applications, text processing, caching layers with moderate write requirements, and lightweight web serving.
